domain: dynamic release nuisance and accessible clone measurement, cycle 4
overall_verdict: plasma-only whole-cell clone growth is exactly non-identifiable under unrestricted time-varying clone-specific release; a standardized cell-associated contrast identifies local relative net growth under static or bounded copy/recovery factors, but the statistical mechanism is standard and not a novelty claim

claims.statement: For observed clone-marker source fluxes F_jl(t)=c_jl q_j(t) X_j(t), arbitrary positive clone-specific release q_j(t) makes cell abundance and relative net growth non-identifiable: for every differentiable phi_j, X'_j=exp(phi_j)X_j and q'_j=exp(-phi_j)q_j preserve all marker source fluxes, and therefore every common-clearance convolution, while changing r_j by phi'_j.
assumptions: positive clone abundance and release on the observed window
all clone-specific marker channels share the clone release factor
clearance acts after marker-specific source generation
claims.novelty_boundary: Gauge symmetry is elementary system identification; no priority claim. It formalizes the exact interface at which plasma-only inference fails.
claims.costs: No finite read depth or number of same-release markers resolves the ambiguity. A clone-specific transfer bound or independent abundance channel must be acquired.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample satisfying the stated observation model where the transformation changes an observable law, or an independently validated release constraint that identifies relative growth without an added state-sensitive channel.
claims.next_gate: Do not infer whole-cell selection from plasma without a finite clone-differential release bound.

claims.statement: In matched cell-associated samples with E[Y_jk]=a_k d_j X_jk, where a_k is sample-wide and d_j is an unknown but invariant clone-specific marker-copy/recovery factor, conditioning within each sample on total clone-marker molecules removes a_k and the time difference in clone log-odds exactly equals the change in cellular log-odds. A randomized treatment-control log-odds contrast equals the treatment effect on relative net growth under constant exponential rates and balanced starting aliquots.
assumptions: two or more measured clone markers cover the compared local population
clone-specific d_j is invariant across the compared arms/times
sample-specific variation is common across clone markers
no differential marker loss or CN drift
constant-rate interpretation only for the stated exponential model
local sample inclusion is the target
claims.status: exact conditional model theorem; no biological validation
claims.novelty_boundary: Conditional multinomial/log-odds cancellation and serial clone-fitness measurements are standard. The design is retained as a useful capability boundary, not a new theorem or assay claim.
claims.costs: Requires repeated representative accessible samples or matched sacrificial culture aliquots, UMI/duplex marker counts, a sample-wide extraction standard, CN/recovery validation, and local spatial sampling. Molecule input scales inversely with marker molecule fraction for fixed detection; small-effect rate estimation scales approximately as 1/(p beta^2).
claims.falsifier: After preregistered CN and recovery stability checks, held-out cell-associated clone odds fail to agree with independent viable-cell or barcode counts.
claims.next_gate: Only pursue as a local preclinical assay design if accessible paired samples or an organoid system are available.

claims.statement: If the differential log marker-copy/recovery factor changes by an unknown amount over the interval, the observed clone log-odds change equals the cellular log-odds change plus that nuisance change; without a finite bound the cellular effect has an unbounded identified set, while a justified absolute drift bound B expands a statistical interval by [-B,+B].
assumptions: same marker identities are measured at both endpoints
the observation equation is multiplicative in clone abundance and marker/recovery factor
the stated bound is externally measured or experimentally justified
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard nuisance partial identification; no novelty claim.
claims.costs: Single-cell CNA/FISH and recovery controls can bound selected nuisance components but do not establish whole-tumour spatial inclusion.
claims.falsifier: A validated assay shows stable inferred cell odds despite an unbounded differential marker/recovery shift under the stated observation model.
claims.next_gate: If the confidence interval expanded by B includes zero, report the growth sign as UNKNOWN.

claims.statement: For a low marker-molecule fraction p and a small treatment log-odds shift beta, the two-sample binomial/logistic contrast has approximate variance 2/(M p); a two-sided 5% test with 80% power therefore requires approximately M >= 15.7/(p beta^2) independent marker opportunities per arm. At least-one-molecule 95% detection requires M >= 2.996/p under the ideal background-free model.
assumptions: low p and local beta approximation
M counts effective independent marker opportunities
claims.status: local asymptotic design calculation plus exact ideal single-molecule sampling threshold
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard binomial/Poisson sampling information; no novelty claim.
claims.costs: The input variable p is marker-molecule fraction, not cell fraction; unknown copy number blocks conversion without calibration. Background and overdispersion increase the budget.
claims.falsifier: Measured held-out power departs materially from the binomial prediction after effective molecule input and assay background are correctly specified.
claims.next_gate: Use molecule-aware power planning before claiming that low-abundance clone trajectories are measurable.

status_note: No empirical data were downloaded or reanalyzed. No whole-tumour, clinical, biological-efficacy, or novelty-priority claim is made.
